answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with identity-bound collateral. Each new agent must lock real stake in a registry that serves as a neutral haven, so forging an identity consumes actual capital. A signed bridge proof ties each deposit to its source chain, so one bond cannot fund many personas. Because the required stake is as scarce and costly as ivory and is slashed on fraud, an attacker must post a fresh, forfeitable bond for every fake agent, making a large Sybil farm prohibitively expensive.
